text: The photographs and the bills of a field visit are rwb-document documents: rwb-partner hands each of them to the rwb-document intake as a claim-check claim (link and manifest, never the bytes), receives a document reference, holds that reference in its answer and its decision record, and writes no document row, no document type, no index entry and no retention itself. No field of partner_instruction carries a document reference, so the reference has no field ID and carries the placeholder.
why: The ownership rows give S9 three tables and none of them is a document; TSD S9 T3.1 defines partner and partner_instruction only and neither has a document column; FSD S9 A2.15.2 names the Workbench document hub as the integration point of the feature and sends attachments to P5 in T5.2; REQ-DCM-013 requires field photographs and bills to reach the same intake and index as scanned documents; and Architecture v5 slide 12 makes a file a claim-check handed over through the file path, never the data. A document column or a document table in S9 would give the service a fourth table no document owns.
read: Context pack ownership rows (tables partner, partner_instruction, partner_user; 6 REST operations); TSD S9 T3.1, T5.2; FSD S9 A2.15.2; LDM v8 document and REQ-DCM-013; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 12; legacy RWB-E7-018 Data; Template and Rules v1 R9
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-document owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The evidence stays one record in one service, this service holds only references, and a build that adds an evidence column or stores document content fails the review

text: The field collector is a partner identity: the field app is a client of the partner gateway of the DMZ (FAPI 2.0) on the caller's firm scope, the caller resolves to one partner_user row bound to one firm and one role over LOV-ROLE with its valid_from and valid_to, and the submission runs under partner portal right U. TSD S9 T6.1 holds no field-collector role, so the role code a field collector holds is Not specified in the source documents; the 13 identities that hold U are the seven RW roles and the six PT roles, which are the eight the legacy permission table names and its five more.
why: FSD S9 A2.15.3.3 makes the field collector the primary role of the feature and TSD S9 T6.1 lists 29 RW and PT identities with no such role; a page of the legacy permission table names eight identities with right U and 'and 5 more'; API-S9-005 declares partner portal right U; and TSD S9 T6.2 scopes every query. Inventing an RW-FIELDCOLLECTOR role or a role code would add a role no document grants, and reading another firm's instruction would break the partner scope.
read: FSD S9 A2.15.3.3; TSD S9 T6.1, T6.2, T-A.1; context pack ownership rows and Architecture v5 slide 8 (partner gateway FAPI 2.0 fronts S9); LDM v8 partner_user DF-REF-212 to DF-REF-217 and LOV-ROLE; legacy RWB-E7-018 Permission checks

confirm: Business lead and the rwb-access owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The submission runs on the caller's firm scope with one role binding, no new role is created, and the role-code list arrives as reference data without a code change

text: The field visit itself is one entry in the interaction ledger of rwb-source-data (P1), with channel VISIT and source FIELD_VISIT, the case, the firm and the contact date, requested on that owner's contract; rwb-partner writes no interaction row, updates no ledger entry and holds no channel value of its own. The operation name and the field that carries the visit reference are Not specified in the source documents.
why: The default ruling of Template and Rules R3 gives the interaction ledger to P1 rwb-source-data and DP-18 is the pattern for it; LDM v8 puts a visit in interaction with DF-INT-005 channel over LOV-CHANNEL (which holds VISIT) and LOV-CONTACT-SRC (which holds FIELD_VISIT); the ownership rows give S9 three tables, none of them an interaction; and the legacy Data table names no visit row at all, so the visit exists as a fact and no service but P1 may hold it.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 DP-18; context pack ownership rows; LDM v8 interaction DF-INT-001 to DF-INT-013, LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-CONTACT-SRC; TSD S9 T3.1 and T5.2; legacy RWB-E7-018 Data
confirm: Solution architect and the rwb-source-data owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: The ledger stays in one service, this service records the visit through a contract, and a build that writes an interaction row here fails the boundary test

text: The outcome of the field work is written on the instruction this service owns: partner_instruction.result_code (DF-PRT-015) holds the result the collector reports and status moves to DONE (DF-PRT-014, LOV-INSTR-STATUS). result_code is a free varchar(40) value with no list in TSD S9 T3.2, so the result vocabulary is Not specified in the source documents and is never declared as an enumeration of the code.
why: TSD S9 T3.1 gives result_code as TEXT varchar(40) with no LOV and T3.2 publishes LOV-INSTR-STATUS, LOV-INSTRUCTION, LOV-PANEL and LOV-PARTNER-TYPE but no result list; the legacy story names no result value either. LOV-INSTR-STATUS already carries DONE, so the status side needs no invention, and a result enumeration would be a business value with no owner.
read: TSD S9 T3.1 (DF-PRT-014, DF-PRT-015), T3.2; FSD S9 A2.15.3.1 (VR-S9-015-1 and BR-S9-015); legacy RWB-E7-018 Data and Acceptance criteria; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01

impact: The result rides one existing column and one existing list value, the vocabulary arrives as data later, and no enumeration is written in code

text: EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted is published by rwb-partner on rwb.partner.events.v1 as rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1 in a CloudEvents 1.0 binary envelope, keyed by the case ID and subject, with the payload instructionId, result, documents and the submitted time, for rwb-case and rwb-reporting. Event and Messaging Design v4 reads the same event as consumed from the partner portal and TSD S9 T5.3 lists it as published; the baseline declares one direction, records the conflict, and the outbox and inbox library of DP-09 is a real dependency the plan's pattern set does not carry.
why: The ownership rows give the service EV-20 and EV-21 and TSD S9 T5.3 lists InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted as published, while the Events sheet reads EV-21 as consumed from the partner portal; in the target the portal and the field app are both REST ingresses and the fact leaves this service. A result recorded without its event would leave rwb-case and rwb-reporting blind, and an event without an outbox row would break the at-least-once rule of ADR-015.
read: Event and Messaging Design v4 events EV-20 and EV-21 and the Events sheet note; TSD S9 T5.3; context pack ownership rows; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09, DP-14 and R7.2 (s12.3)
confirm: Solution architect and the event platform owner, before wave 4 starts
impact: One event on one topic with one direction, the case and the reporting read model are told the same day, and the DP-09 dependency is recorded rather than added to the metadata table

text: No partner route set exists, so the decision record of the field work carries the rule ID and the version in force as the rwb-decision contract supplies them and no rule row, package or rule ID set is declared; the nearest rows of the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 are R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39 and R-UNI-40, and the rule ID and its version carry the placeholder until a partner route set is published.
why: Legacy AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version and DP-03 requires the rule ID and the version; the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 holds restructure, guarantee, litigation, asset disposal, debt sale, write-off, deviation, universal and deed in lieu route sets and no PRM set, and R-UNI-38 to R-UNI-40 speak of a version's effective date, a failed log write and a duplicate event, not of a field visit. Citing them as the rule of the visit would misattribute a platform rule, and inventing an ID would create a row no business owner approved.

text: The five legacy states of PRT-02 — New, accepted, in progress, result and closed — are the screen's words for SENT, ACCEPTED, IN_PROGRESS and DONE of LOV-INSTR-STATUS, with New at SENT and result and closed both at DONE; DECLINED and RECALLED are values of the list with no screen state of their own, and no source describes the words, the field list or the offline indicator of the field-app form.
why: The legacy screen table gives PRT-02 five states and TSD S9 T3.2 publishes six list values in a different vocabulary; two of the legacy words (result, closed) map to one list value and two list values have no legacy word, so a one-to-one mapping does not exist. Treating closed as a seventh status would add a value no list holds, and inventing the form's words would add screen text no source owns.
read: Legacy RWB-E7-018 Screen and states; FSD S9 Screens table (PRT-02 Instruction, PRT-03 Upload result); TSD S9 T3.2 (LOV-INSTR-STATUS); Template and Rules v1 R7.2 (s15)

text: The field application is a client of the partner gateway of the DMZ (FAPI 2.0) and of API-S9-005 on the caller's firm scope: it has no interface ID of its own, its offline capture and its upload on reconnect are the client's queue plus the service's idempotent repeat of the same Idempotency-Key, and its devices, its media types, its size limits and its per-submission file count are Not specified in the source documents. NFR-062 and NFR-063 stay at Proposed under DL11 and this story fixes no target for them.

Declaring an INT id would create a register entry no owner holds, and writing a target value would answer DL11 by guessing.
